name: Sonnet+tools small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Long-only basket of small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech growth names sized by current momentum and stress-window resilience, with a cash buffer.
reassessment_note: This week clearly separated the book's five names on fundamentals and price action, so I re-sized by momentum rather than holding blind. Samsara (IOT) and Rubrik (RBRK) both delivered strong Q2 prints with raised forward guidance and fresh sell-side upgrades: Samsara raised FY guidance to ~$2.05B on 30% revenue growth with large-customer/AI-product expansion, and BNP Paribas lifted its target from $40 to $55 while RBC flagged more growth ahead from large customers, AI, and international demand -- the stock closed +3.74% on Thursday and is +13.4% YTD. Rubrik beat with 38% revenue growth, raised FY27 guidance, and struck a new CrowdStrike AI-security partnership, closing +1.66% on Thursday even after profit-taking pared back August's 28.6% surge. Affirm is the opposite story this week: fiscal Q4 revenue and GMV both grew strongly (+33%/+36%) but the stock still sold off -4% on the print and is down -6.96% over the past five trading days on rising delinquency/credit-quality concerns flagged explicitly by the CEO, even though sell-side price targets (BofA $104, Truist $85) remain well above the current $72.35 mark -- that's a real near-term momentum problem despite a still-constructive longer-run analyst view, so I'm trimming it rather than holding full size or exiting outright. Flywire is a modest trim: no negative fundamental news, but a 10%-owner sold $840K of stock this week and the name lacks a fresh catalyst versus its faster-moving basket-mates. Toast is roughly unchanged -- steady 23% revenue growth and raised guidance, offset by continued insider (CFO) selling and a full valuation -- so I'm leaving it near its prior small size. Net effect: shift weight from the weakest-momentum name (AFRM) into the two names with the freshest positive catalysts and guidance raises (IOT, RBRK), trim the quieter/insider-selling names modestly (FLYW), and nudge cash up slightly given Monday's holiday closure ahead of Tuesday's entry and the mixed credit-quality signal now sitting inside the fintech leg.

positions.thesis: Best momentum and cleanest catalyst set in the book this week: Q2 revenue +30% YoY to $508.4M, FY guidance raised to ~$2.05B, large-customer and AI-product expansion cited as the driver, stock +3.74% Thursday and +13.4% YTD, with BNP raising its target from $40 to $55 (~37% above the $40.20 mark) and RBC constructive on continued large-customer/AI/international growth. Sizing up from 22% to the book's largest position to let the strongest momentum name run.

Q2 beat with 38% revenue growth and a raised FY27 guide, plus a new CrowdStrike AI-security automation partnership that extends the product moat; stock +1.66% Thursday and holding most of August's 28.6% run despite some post-earnings profit-taking on free-cash-flow-margin questions (15%). Sizing up from 14% to 20% on the guidance raise and durable partnership news, while keeping a wide stop given the name's volatility (42-108 52-week range).

Fundamentals are still growing fast (fiscal Q4 revenue +33%, GMV +36%) and sell-side price targets (BofA $104, Truist $85) sit well above the $72.35 mark, but the stock is down -6.96% over the past five sessions and fell -4% on the print itself as the CEO flagged rising consumer delinquency pressure -- a real near-term momentum and credit-quality headwind for a BNPL name. Trimming from 26% to 16% rather than exiting: the growth story is intact but this is not a week to be the book's largest position.

No adverse fundamental news, but a 10%-owner reported an $840K stock sale this week and the name has no fresh growth catalyst versus its faster-moving basket-mates right now. Trimming modestly from 10% to 8% to fund the higher-conviction adds while keeping exposure to cross-border payments growth.

Steady execution continues (Q2 revenue +23% YoY, raised guidance, expanding AI capabilities) and the stock was flat on the week, but continued CFO insider selling and a full valuation keep this a small, non-conviction-add position. Holding near prior size (5% -> 6%) rather than pressing it.
